messages.subject: Access nimbleList
parts:
I study the use of nimbleList on page 165 of the manual. I have pasted my example code below.

First question:
I want to create the "la_index". Because the varying "K" can change the size and indices (for indicating the parameter location in the model), I found I need to use "eval" to get "la_index". I wonder if there is a smarter way to do this in short.

Second question:
I can access the list elements by, for example, "la_index$v1". I wonder if I can assess by something like "la_index[[1]]". Then assess "la_index$v1" by "la_index[[2]]", and so on. It is much more convenient to use "[[1]]", "[[2]]" than to use "v1", "v2", and so on, because my "la_index" is varying in length for different "K".

Thank you for developing such a great NIMBLE package. I learn a lot from it and enjoy using it for parameter estimation!

Keith


K = 4
    # nimble code
    require("nimble")
    require("evaluate")
   
    # Create indices of main, interaction effects as nimbleList: la_index
    library("utils")
    la_index_mat = la_index_list = vector("list",K)
    v = character(K)
    for (k in 1:K){
      la_index_mat[[k]] = combn(1:K,k)
      v[k] = paste("v",as.character(k),sep="")
      la_index_list[[k]] = nimbleType(name = v[k], type = 'double', dim = 2)
    }
    la_index_list_def <- nimbleList(la_index_list)
    txt = character()
    for (k in 1:K){
      if (k==1){point = ""}else{point = ", "}
      txt = paste(txt, point, v[k]," = la_index_mat[[",as.character(k),"]]", sep="")
    }
    txt = paste("la_index = la_index_list_def$new(",txt,")",sep="")
    eval(parse(text=txt))

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Access nimbleList
parts:
Keith, I'm not exactly sure about the application, but the following does the same thing in somewhat less code:

K <- 4
la_index_list <- lapply(1:K, function(k) nimbleType(name = paste0('v',k), type = 'double', dim = 2))
la_index_list_def <- nimbleList(la_index_list)
argList <- lapply(1:K, function(k) combn(1:K,k))
names(argList) <- paste0('v', 1:K)
la_index <- do.call(la_index_list_def$new, argList)

As for your second question, unfortunately no, you need to use the names (e.g., "v1" or "v2") to access the elements.

Another approach to doing this, for variable length K and access using index number, could be using a nimbleFunctionList, where each element in the nimbleFunctIonList is a nimbleFunction with one member data element (to hold the 2x2 matrices), and a method called (for example) getMatrix.  Then, you could access the K matices as:

my_nimbleFunctionList[[1]]$getMatrix()
my_nimbleFunctionList[[2]]$getMatrix()
## etc...

Hope this helps,
Daniel
